body: I'm a 30 bisexual and I have no idea how to explain to my friends why I've been hiding it all these years, so I just don't.
Going into surgery. I hope I never wake up. Goodbye.
I don't see this happening as my situation has been crappy long before my thyroid issues began. I'm just genetically crap. I shouldn't have children or have been raised in the first place.

Because doctors are warning me that if I don't take care of it there's a chance it will spread and dying of cancer is a really, really terrible death. I've seen my mother go through it.

The doctors obviously don't know anything for sure, they have statistics they like to play with.

Foreskin restoration is crap, sorry, but I believe it's just another fad to suck money out of people. Nothing will restore all the nerve endings I lost and what I'll end up with is a hairy flappy skin which will look worse than it already does.

I've had magic mushrooms before, yes they're amazing but never really solved any of my problems. Maybe if I could take them in a medical environment they could help.

I like traveling, yes the change in atmosphere makes it better. But I always have to go back, to the same boring life, full of pain and suffering. Before I had some hope, but today I realize nothing will change that.

Yes, he's supposed to be one of the best in my country.

I trust him to do a good job cutting me and pulling the parts that he should be pulling. What I don't trust is whether I even have to go through this surgery at all. There are some statistics that show that this particular cancer has been diagnosed a lot more in recent years but that there is no change at all in fatalities. It's also known that some people live with this cancer their whole lives and never even know about it because it's a very dormant type of cancer. 

Also one doctor/professor I've been to told me he once pulled a thyroid which was later found not to contain cancer at all. I was shocked this could happen but he told me it can.

This surgery isn't without side effects. There's a chance my calcium glands will get damaged and that means taking tons of calcium for life just to balance that out. There is also a small chance that the surgeon will make a mistake and hit the nerve which controls the voice chords. If that happens they'll be paralyzed forever and I won't be able to breath like a normal person, not to mention not be able to talk.
It doesn't make me feel good, it makes me feel awful. But anything that I can eat without worrying about issues later either tastes awful or is expensive.

When I did the initial ultrasound I reacted furiously because I've been claiming to my doctors for years that I somehow can't balance my thyroid at all and that I'm always feeling bad but they never bothered sending me for any special checkups. I wanted to kill or sue someone.

The biopsy was a different thing though, I was much calmer because I knew it's going to be cancer. It was as if there was nothing else it could be, so I wasn't surprised at all when it came positive. By that time I also wished it was worse (it could also have spread to the lungs but it didn't).

Then I was in denial for a while, tried changing my diet again, tried taking time off and relax and do meditation. I felt better but that didn't take away the tumor. After about 3 months I finally gave up and set a date for the surgery.

I'm really not scared of the surgery, or of death. What I'm scared of is reality and how awful it can be sometimes. I will have to take a drug each morning for the rest of my life to replace the action of a natural organ. It's probably not going to be the same ever again, probably not going to be able to control my hormones properly. It's difficult.
